content.text: The text reviews intestinal indigestion, constipation, colic, acute/chronic intestinal catarrh, cholera morbus, and summer diarrhoea in infants. Causes include overeating, poor chewing, unsuitable or contaminated food and water, alcohol, irregular meals, inactivity, constipation, disease of the liver, pancreas, heart, or lungs, and hot weather with foul air. Symptoms range from gas, abdominal pain, altered stools, diarrhoea, fever, anaemia, wasting, and nervous disturbance to collapse and obstruction. Diagnosis depends on history, examination, stool characteristics, and distinguishing gastric, hepatic, pancreatic, infectious, and structural disease. Treatment emphasizes rest in bed, careful diet, hydration, hygiene, gradual exercise, and avoiding indiscriminate purgatives; medicines and enemas are secondary. Patients may benefit from travel or relocation to cool, dry mountains, the seashore, countryside, or European and American mineral springs; children are sometimes sent to the country.
